articles.title: What happened at IIT Mandi? Inquiry ordered after Bhagavad Gita-themed poster sparks caste discrimination row
articles.summary: News News: IIT Mandi has found itself at the centre of a controversy after a Bhagavad Gita-themed poster displayed on the campus during Janmashtami celebrations .
articles.body: IIT Mandi has found itself at the centre of a controversy after a Bhagavad Gita-themed poster displayed on the campus during Janmashtami celebrations described the role of Shudras as being to “serve higher classes." The wording triggered allegations of caste discrimination and prompted the institute to order an inquiry into how the poster was prepared and displayed.The controversy has also drawn attention to IIT Mandi Director Laxmidhar Behera's long association with teachings based on the Bhagavad Gita and ISKCON. However, Behera has strongly distanced the institute from the poster, saying it was part of a student-led event and had not received institutional approval.Poster displayed during Janmashtami celebrations sparks controversyThe poster, titled “Bhagavad Gita—The Timeless Wisdom," was displayed outside IIT Mandi's auditorium during Janmashtami celebrations on September 4.It sought to explain the four divisions of society referred to in the Bhagavad Gita, Brahmanas, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, and Shudras. The poster described Brahmanas as those who “spread God's message," Kshatriyas as those who “protect society and spirituality," and Vaishyas as those who “drive the economy and support others."However, the description assigned to Shudras, "serve higher classes," triggered outrage and became the central point of the controversy.The poster also carried a verse from the Bhagavad Gita referring to the four divisions of human society being created according to the “three modes of material nature and the work associated with them."The display raised concerns among members of the academic community and others who viewed the wording as reinforcing caste hierarchy and discrimination.IIT Mandi director condemns the displayResponding to the controversy, IIT Mandi Director Laxmidhar Behera said he was “shocked” after learning about the poster and made it clear that the institute had not approved or endorsed it, according to TNN.In an email sent to the IIT Mandi community on Sunday, Behera described his response as an “outright condemnation of recent poster display within campus." He said the institute was committed to the constitutional principles of equality, social justice, and scientific temper.“The institute strongly condemns any form of caste-based discrimination,” Bahera told PTI, while urging members of the campus community to stand united against discrimination and social bias.Behera also said he personally empathised with members of the IIT Mandi community who had been hurt by the incident.Inquiry committee set up to examine the matterThe IIT Mandi administration has now constituted an inquiry committee to investigate the circumstances surrounding the poster.According to Behera, the committee includes faculty members as well as representatives from different social groups, including members of the Scheduled Castes and Other Backward Classes.The panel will examine how the poster was prepared, who authorised its display and how it eventually became part of the student-led Janmashtami event.Behera told PTI that he had been away from the campus when the poster was displayed and returned on Saturday. He said he learnt about the controversy on Sunday morning.“I have not seen the poster. I don't want to take a side here and let the panel decide,” he told PTI.Director's association with Bhagavad Gita draws attentionThe controversy has also brought renewed attention to Behera's association with the Bhagavad Gita and ISKCON.According to his official IIT Mandi profile, Behera has spent nearly three decades teaching what he describes as universal principles of peace through the Bhagavad Gita. He is also associated with the proposed Bhaktivedanta University, described on its website as an ISKCON initiative.Behera currently teaches a three-credit course on the Bhagavad Gita at IIT Mandi.Amid questions surrounding the poster, he defended ISKCON's position on caste discrimination, maintaining that the organisation opposes casteism and promotes equality.He told PTI that occupational duties, according to his understanding, are determined by guna and karma, rather than caste-based discrimination.Behera also pointed to what he described as increased representation of marginalised communities among the institute's faculty during his tenure.Previous controversies involving the IIT Mandi directorThis is not the first time Behera's views have attracted public attention. In 2023, he reportedly asked students to take a pledge against eating meat and linked extreme weather events, including landslides and cloudbursts in Himachal Pradesh, to cruelty towards animals.Earlier, in 2022, a video surfaced in which he spoke about using the chanting of holy mantras to help a friend's family deal with what he described as “evil spirits”.More recently, IIT Mandi's Indian Knowledge System and Mental Health Applications Centre organised a conference that included discussions on subjects such as the Bhagavad Gita, Ayurveda and reincarnation. Behera was among those associated with the event and also co-organised a session dealing with reincarnation, out-of-body experiences and afterlife communication.What happens next?For now, the focus remains on the inquiry ordered by IIT Mandi. The committee is expected to establish how the controversial poster was created and displayed on the campus and whether any institutional procedures were bypassed.The incident has once again raised a larger question about the responsibility of educational institutions when religious, cultural, or philosophical ideas are presented in academic spaces. While IIT Mandi has unequivocally stated that it does not support caste-based discrimination, the findings of its inquiry will be closely watched to determine how the controversial display found a place on one of India's premier technical campuses.As the investigation proceeds, the controversy has underlined the sensitivity surrounding caste, religion, and social equality, particularly within educational institutions that are expected to uphold the constitutional values of inclusion and equal opportunity.(With inputs from PTI)Get the latest Education News and Live updates. articles.title: Alleged cryptoscam ringleader set for plea hearing in $240M bitcoin theft
articles.summary: Malone Lam allegedly used a social engineering attack to steal over 4,100 Bitcoin, then blew millions on Lamborghinis, nightclubs and mansions.
articles.body: A 22-year-old Singapore man accused of helping steal more than $240 million in Bitcoin from a single victim and splurging the proceeds on luxury cars, private jets, mansions and wild nights out is expected to plead guilty this week in one of the largest cryptocurrency thefts in U.S. history. Malone Lam, an eighth-grade dropout from Singapore whom prosecutors have identified as a suspected ringleader of the sprawling cryptocurrency scheme, is scheduled for a plea agreement hearing Tuesday in federal court in Washington, D.C. Lam and his alleged co-conspirators were part of an alleged network of young men in their late teens and early 20s who prosecutors say used a sophisticated "social engineering" attack in August 2024 to trick a wealthy, longtime cryptocurrency investor into handing over access to his digital holdings. GLOBAL TASK FORCE DISMANTLES 'PIG-BUTCHERING' CRYPTO FRAUD RINGS PREYING ON AMERICANS According to prosecutors, members of the group contacted the victim while posing as representatives of Google and the Gemini cryptocurrency exchange, warning him that his accounts had been compromised. The scammers allegedly convinced the victim to give them access to his Google Drive and provide security codes that allowed Lam and others to siphon off more than 4,100 Bitcoin, then worth over $240 million. The group allegedly moved the stolen cryptocurrency through multiple exchange platforms and used money laundering specialists to convert portions of it into cash. Prosecutors say Lam and his associates then embarked on a staggering spending spree. Lam and his friends allegedly spent $4 million at Los Angeles nightclubs in roughly a month, including more than $569,000 that Lam allegedly spent during a single night out. He also allegedly used stolen cryptocurrency to purchase a $2 million watch and more than 30 vehicles, including custom Porsches, Lamborghinis and Ferraris. The group also rented multimillion-dollar homes, flew on private jets and hired private security. The alleged spending was so lavish that the judge overseeing Lam's initial court appearance in Miami invoked a famous Hollywood troublemaker after hearing a prosecutor describe it. "I could only think of Ferris Bueller gone bad," U.S. Magistrate Judge Alicia Valle said, referring to the school-skipping protagonist of the 1986 movie "Ferris Bueller's Day Off." FBI WRAPS UP CYBERCRIME OPERATION TARGETING GLOBAL NETWORKS PREYING ON AMERICANS The lavish lifestyle quickly attracted attention as investigators closed in. One alleged co-conspirator, Jeandiel Serrano, failed to conceal his IP address while creating an account on a cryptocurrency exchange that held nearly $30 million in stolen funds, prosecutors said. Investigators traced the address to an Encino, California, home Serrano was renting for $47,500 per month. Serrano and Lam were arrested separately on Sept. 18, 2024. FBI agents took Serrano into custody at Los Angeles International Airport, where authorities said he was wearing a watch worth roughly $500,000. Lam was arrested the same day at a Miami mansion. Eighteen defendants have been charged in connection with the case, with ten already pleading guilty. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP At Lam's initial court appearance, a prosecutor estimated that federal sentencing guidelines could call for a prison term of at least 14 years if he is convicted. articles.title: Arrestan a los 95 años a Bernie Ecclestone, exjefe de la Fórmula 1, en su viaje a Portugal: llevaba un rifle no declarado en la maleta
articles.standfirst: Fue detenido por la policía aeroportuaria en Cascais, donde aterrizó con su avión privado procedente de Suiza
articles.summary: Fue detenido por la policía aeroportuaria en Cascais, donde aterrizó con su avión privado procedente de Suiza
articles.body: La edad nunca es un obstáculo para nada. Si no que se lo pregunten a Bernie Ecclestone que a sus 95 años ha vuelto a ser noticia, pero en esta ocasión lejos de sus anteriores responsabilidades en el mundo del motor. Según informes locales, el histórico magnate y exjefe comercial de la Fórmula 1 fue arrestado en Portugal por portar ilegalmente un rifle. Una detención que se habría producido durante un control rutinario en el aeropuerto de Tires, en Cascais, tras aterrizar a bordo de su jet privado procedente de Saanen (Suiza), donde el empresario británico posee un chalet. Todo empezó como siempre que un avión quiere tocar tierra después de un vuelo. Los radares detectaron la llegada de la aeronave a la terminal portuguesa a las 10:55 a. m. del lunes y fue justo después de ese instante cuando los agentes de la División Aeroportuaria de la Policía de Seguridad Pública (PSP) realizaron las inspecciones pertinentes al equipaje e interceptaron el arma sin registrar. Aunque la noticia ha trascendido rápidamente en los medios internacionales, las autoridades policiales lusas aún no han emitido un comunicado oficial confirmando los detalles del procedimiento. No es la primera vez que el magnate se ve envuelto en un incidente de esta naturaleza. En mayo de 2022, Ecclestone ya fue arrestado por la policía en el aeropuerto de Campinas, en Brasil, cuando se disponía a abordar un vuelo privado llevando consigo una pistola LW Seecamp 32 indocumentada. En aquella ocasión, el empresario afirmó desconocer que el arma estaba dentro de su equipaje antes de facturar. Durante aquel episodio en el país sudamericano, la Oficina de Seguridad Pública del Estado de São Paulo confirmó la intervención. Ecclestone pudo ser puesto en libertad y continuar su viaje hacia Suiza tras abonar una fianza de 6.000 reales brasileños (alrededor de 1.150 euros) y la confiscación del arma. Más tarde, quitó importancia al asunto calificándolo como un "incidente tonto e insignificante" y asegurando que simplemente había sido interrogado. El exdirigente de la F1 explicó entonces que había adquirido aquella pistola años atrás a un mecánico del gran circo como medida de disuasión. Sin embargo, este nuevo hallazgo en el aeródromo portugués vuelve a colocar al veterano multimillonario en el centro de la polémica policial y mediática por reincidir en la transportación irregular de armas de fuego en sus vuelos privados.

articles.title: Next wins key appeal to overturn £30m equal pay ruling
articles.summary: A judge ruled Next can pay warehouse workers more because it is harder to recruit and retain them.
articles.body:
Next has won an appeal allowing it to keep paying warehouse workers a higher hourly rate than shop floor staff in a long running battle over equal pay.

The Employment Appeal Tribunal has overturned a key part of a landmark ruling in 2024 which found the retailer was wrong to pay its warehouse staff higher basic pay than shop floor workers for jobs of equal value.

More than 3,500 current and former employees, mainly women, had been set to share potentially more than £30m in back pay as a result of that judgement.

After Next's appeal, the law firm Leigh Day, which represents store workers, described the conclusion on basic pay as "disappointing" and said it will appeal the decision.

The tribunal accepted that Next was justified in paying higher rates because of recruitment and retention pressures for warehouse workers.

Next described the decision as a "landmark victory" succeeding on the "key issue of basic pay".

In a statement, it said: "The importance of this decision is that the Appeal Tribunal has confirmed that it was justifiable for Next to rely on market forces to distinguish between different groups of employees, where there was a good rationale to pay one group more than the other.

"In this case, Next had to pay a higher market rate to warehouse operatives because of recruitment and retention pressures, which did not apply to the workforce in its stores. Next believes this element of the judgment is not only correct in law, but also a victory for common sense.

"The judgment affirms a principle at the heart of any effective employment market - that employers must be able to pay what is necessary to recruit the people they need; and that doing so does not oblige them to raise the pay of other employees where there is no reason to do so."

Leigh Day said judges did uphold 2024 findings on night-time premiums, overtime premiums and paid rest breaks.

Next said it will now seek permission to appeal these decisions.

Both the original Employment Tribunal and the Appeal Tribunal found there was no direct sex discrimination in Next's pay rates. Shop floor staff are predominantly women while warehouse workers are predominantly male.

Questions are now being asked about if this result could set a precedent across the industry. Tesco, Asda, Morrisons, and Sainbury's are all involved in similar long running claims and will be studying the findings closely.

Last year, thousands of female workers at Birmingham City Council heard how much money they will receive in a long-awaited equal pay settlement. Brighton and Hove City Council is also facing over 1,000 equal pay cases.

articles.title: Ritzy Miami steakhouse manager held on ICE detainer after mom found stabbed to death
articles.summary: Surveillance video allegedly shows the Miami steakhouse manager blood-soaked in an elevator with a knife hours after returning home with his mother.
articles.body: A Miami steakhouse manager allegedly emerged from his luxury apartment covered in blood and clutching a knife before telling police he had acted in self-defense after his mother was found stabbed to death inside. Stefano Eduardo Cremasco-Cicero, 36, told officers, "I was defending myself," after Miami police were called to the Brickell high-rise early Friday, according to an arrest report obtained by WPLG. Cremasco-Cicero is charged with second-degree murder with a weapon, Miami-Dade County jail records show. KARMELO ANTHONY STAYS SILENT AS ANALYSTS WARN DEFENSE FACES UPHILL BATTLE IN TRACK MEET STABBING TRIAL Officers were dispatched at about 4:47 a.m. for an "unknown request for police assistance," according to the outlet. Officers found Cremasco-Cicero in the lobby with blood on his hands, clothing and shoes, the outlet reported. He allegedly directed officers upstairs to the apartment. Inside the apartment, police found his mother lying behind the front door with multiple apparent stab wounds, according to WPLG. Miami Fire Rescue pronounced her dead shortly after 5 a.m. FLORIDA MAN ACCUSED OF KILLING MOM AND BURNING BODY BECAUSE SHE ‘WANTED TO BE CREMATED’ Authorities have not publicly identified the woman or disclosed her age. Police said she was visiting from Mexico and staying with her son. The unusual chain of events began when a food delivery driver arrived at the building and encountered Cremasco-Cicero in the lobby, according to the report. He allegedly opened the door for the driver and asked her to call 911. Cremasco-Cicero ultimately placed the call himself but handed the phone to the woman so she could give the dispatcher the building information, WPLG reported. The driver noticed blood on him as they waited for police, according to the outlet. When she tried to return his phone, he allegedly refused to take it, and she later handed it to responding officers. THE SURVEILLANCE CAMERA ON YOUR STREET CORNER: LAWFUL SPYING OR CONSTITUTIONALLY PROBLEMATIC? Investigators then turned to surveillance video and building access records to piece together what happened in the hours before police arrived. Surveillance video showed Cremasco-Cicero and his mother returning to the building together at about 10:32 p.m. Thursday, according to WPLG. They were reportedly alone in the elevator. COURTNEY CLENNEY'S DEFENSE INSPECTS KNIVES AT CENTER OF ONLYFANS MODEL'S MURDER CASE AHEAD OF TRIAL: REPORT At about 4:26 a.m., surveillance video allegedly captured Cremasco-Cicero entering an elevator wearing a white shirt, khaki pants and white shoes that appeared to be covered in blood. Police said he was carrying a knife. He allegedly dropped the knife after stepping out of the elevator, picked it back up and rode another elevator upstairs, according to the report. Investigators said Cremasco-Cicero later reappeared in a different, long-sleeved blue shirt and walked out of the building while using his phone. He returned minutes later and sat on a couch in the lobby before flagging down the delivery driver, WPLG reported. Police said Cremasco-Cicero had small cuts on his hands and blood residue on his body and clothing. Crime scene investigators photographed him and collected his clothes, according to the outlet. 5 REASONS MORE AMERICANS ARE CUTTING OFF THEIR OWN PARENTS, ACCORDING TO PSYCHOLOGIST After obtaining a search warrant, homicide detectives allegedly recovered several kitchen knives with blood on them, blood-spattered shirts, broken glass and a broken wine bottle from the apartment, WPLG reported. Cremasco-Cicero’s wife told detectives she was in France attending a wedding when the killing happened, according to the report. She said her husband and his mother had not been close since his parents divorced and that he had recently been under stress while preparing to open a restaurant in Coconut Grove. The Miami Herald identified Cremasco-Cicero as the U.S. operating manager of the high-end 1986 Steakhouse in Miami. The arrest report identified Cremasco-Cicero as a Miami resident through an investor visa, according to WPLG. Miami-Dade Corrections records reviewed by Fox News Digital show Cremasco-Cicero was booked Friday night and is being held at the Turner Guilford Knight Correctional Center. The records list no bond, a domestic-violence designation and a hold for immigration authorities. The jail record does not provide additional details about the immigration hold. A Department of Homeland Security spokesperson confirmed to Fox News Digital that Cremasco-Cicero is an illegal immigrant. "On August 5, 2026, ICE lodged a detainer for Stefano Eduardo Cremasco Cicero, a criminal illegal alien from Mexico, charged with homicide," the DHS spokesperson said. "We are calling on Florida to honor our detainer. His claims will be heard by an immigration judge and he will receive due process. This administration will not ignore the rule of law." "Under President Trump and Secretary Mullin, if you break the law, you will face the consequences," the spokesperson added. "Criminal illegal aliens are not welcome in the U.S." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP A motive for the killing remains unclear. Fox News Digital reached out to the Miami Police Department, the Miami-Dade Clerk of Courts and 1986 Steakhouse for additional information.

articles.title: Supporters of Alabama school bus driver charged in deadly accident say she suffered from 'medical crisis'
articles.summary: Theresa McCloud faces vehicular homicide charges after a fatal Auburn school bus crash, but supporters claim a sudden blood sugar drop caused the accident.
articles.body: An Alabama woman accused of causing a deadly crash while driving a school bus experienced a medical crisis during the accident, her supporters reportedly said. Theresa McCloud, 75, faces charges of vehicular homicide and criminal negligence for the Nov. 18, 2025 crash in Auburn. McCloud was driving a bus for Auburn City Schools when she struck a vehicle. Jennifer Leigh Cooper, 42, a well-known local bakery owner, was killed in the collision, AL.com reported. HEART-STOPPING VIDEO SHOWS MIDDLE SCHOOLERS SAVING THEIR BUS AFTER DRIVER PASSES OUT AT THE WHEEL McCloud's supporters said she suffered a medical crisis during the fatal crash. However, a lawsuit filed by Cooper's husband against McCloud and the Auburn City Schools Board of Education alleges that McCloud had diabetes and had been prescribed opiates. On the day of the accident, McCloud told her supervisors that she was not feeling well, the lawsuit states. Two days prior, she had visited a doctor who prescribed opiates to help with her symptoms. Those medications came with a warning label against driving while taking them, according to the suit. "Theresa’s blood sugar suddenly dropped to 23 mg/dL while driving, causing confusion and loss of consciousness," stated a GoFundMe page that has since been removed. OLDER ADULTS TAKING 5 OR MORE PRESCRIPTION DRUGS FACE HIGHER RISK OF DEATH, STUDY FINDS "Theresa had never experienced a low blood sugar episode before, and doctors confirmed that this was a medical crisis," the page continued. "Even so, Theresa is now facing the overwhelming challenge of defending against charges connected to that emergency. On September 4, 2026, Theresa turned herself in and began facing the legal process head-on." While driving, McCloud lost control "based on either her known medical conditions, her use of opiates and/or a mix of both," the lawsuit alleges. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The suit further said that the opiates and her diabetes "severely impaired her ability to drive any vehicle and made her unable to perform her duties as a bus driver," according to the newspaper. McCloud's family reportedly disputes the allegations. Fox News Digital has reached out to the school district.

articles.title: Los Mossos persiguen un coche por un supuesto secuestro en Lleida y descubren que se trataba de una despedida de soltero
articles.standfirst: Varios testigos alertaron al 112 después de ver a un grupo de jóvenes encapuchados atar de pies y manos a otro chico y meterlo en el maletero de un vehículo
articles.summary: Varios testigos alertaron al 112 después de ver a un grupo de jóvenes encapuchados atar de pies y manos a otro chico y meterlo en el maletero de un vehículo
articles.body: Una llamada de varios vecinos al teléfono de emergencias 112 puso en alerta a los Mossos d'Esquadra por un supuesto secuestro en la localidad ilerdense de Cervera. Los testigos aseguraron haber visto a un grupo de cuatro o cinco jóvenes encapuchados atar de pies y manos a otro chico en plena calle y, posteriormente, introducirlo en el maletero de un Jaguar de color blanco. Además, advirtieron de que los supuestos secuestradores llevaban una pistola. Ante la gravedad de la información, los Mossos d'Esquadra activaron un dispositivo para tratar de localizar el coche, que constaba domiciliado en Lleida. Desde la Región Policial de Ponent se establecieron varios puntos estratégicos de control y se difundieron entre las patrullas y las diferentes salas policiales tanto las características del coche como la matrícula facilitada por los testigos. La información se transmitió rápidamente por la emisora de los agentes y, alrededor de las 21.00 horas, varias patrullas consiguieron localizar el vehículo. Los policías iniciaron entonces el seguimiento del vehículo hasta que pudieron detenerlo en la carretera L-313, en el cruce con la C-1412a, cerca de Ponts, en la comarca de la Noguera. Los agentes identificaron a los ocupantes e inspeccionaron el vehículo ante la posibilidad de que se encontraran ante un secuestro. Sin embargo, la investigación sobre el terreno permitió descubrir que la escena no tenía relación con ninguna actividad criminal. Durante el registro, los Mossos d'Esquadra encontraron un cuchillo y una pistola de plástico. La explicación de los jóvenes terminó de aclarar el misterio: se trataba de una despedida de soltero y el supuesto secuestro formaba parte de una broma que los amigos habían preparado para el novio. Aunque finalmente todo quedó en un susto, el episodio obligó a los Mossos d'Esquadra a movilizar un dispositivo policial ante la posibilidad de que se tratara de un secuestro real. Según informa ElCaso.com, los agentes llegaron a valorar inicialmente que pudiera tratarse incluso de un incidente relacionado con el tráfico de drogas, debido a los antecedentes de detenciones ilegales vinculadas a grupos criminales dedicados al narcotráfico. Lo que comenzó con una llamada de emergencia y un operativo policial terminó, finalmente, como una peculiar anécdota de despedida de soltero que los protagonistas difícilmente olvidarán.
